faqs.q: How much does a Working Kelpie cost to buy?
faqs.a: Reputable breeders typically charge $800–$3,000 for a Working Kelpie puppy. Prices vary by breeder reputation, health testing, and lineage. Rescue adoption fees are typically $100–$500 and include vaccinations, neutering, and microchipping.

faqs.q: What is the monthly cost of owning a Working Kelpie?
faqs.a: Budget $150–$300 per month for a Working Kelpie, covering food, preventive vet care, insurance, grooming and supplies. Mid-size breeds sit in the moderate cost range across most ownership categories.

faqs.q: What are the biggest ongoing costs for a Working Kelpie?
faqs.a: The three largest annual expenses are food ($500–900), veterinary care ($400–$1,200 budgeted annually), and pet insurance ($$400–$1,200 per year). Grooming costs are lower for short-coated breeds managed at home.

faqs.q: How much does a Working Kelpie cost in the first year?
faqs.a: Year one costs for a Working Kelpie are significantly higher than subsequent years, typically $2,000–$4,000. This covers the purchase price or adoption fee, initial vet checks, vaccinations, spay/neuter, microchipping, crate, bedding, collar, leads and puppy training classes.

faqs.q: How often should I groom a Working Kelpie?
faqs.a: Working Kelpies need brushing 3–5 times per week, daily during seasonal coat blows. The dense undercoat requires a dedicated undercoat rake, not just a surface slicker brush. Nails should be trimmed every 3–4 weeks. Ears should be checked and cleaned monthly.

faqs.q: Do Working Kelpies shed a lot?
faqs.a: Working Kelpies have seasonal shedding — manageable with a consistent brushing routine.

faqs.q: What grooming tools does a Working Kelpie need?
faqs.a: A slicker brush for surface debris and an undercoat rake for the dense undercoat are both essential. A shedding blade or deshedding tool helps during heavy moult periods. A nail grinder is useful if your Working Kelpie is sensitive to clippers.

faqs.q: How often should I bathe a Working Kelpie?
faqs.a: Every 4–6 weeks is appropriate for most Working Kelpies that live indoors. More frequent bathing is needed if they swim or spend time in mud. Over-bathing strips natural skin oils — use a pH-balanced dog shampoo rather than human products.

faqs.q: Are Working Kelpies easy to train?
faqs.a: Working Kelpies are independent thinkers and can be challenging to train. They respond best to high-value rewards and clear, consistent criteria. A structured puppy class from week one is strongly recommended.

faqs.q: What training method works best for a Working Kelpie?
faqs.a: Reward-based training using treats, praise and toy rewards is the most effective and well-researched approach for Working Kelpies. Clicker training with precise timing works well to mark the exact moment of correct behaviour. Avoid aversive methods — they increase anxiety and often create secondary behavioural problems.

faqs.q: At what age should I start training my Working Kelpie?
faqs.a: Start training from the day your puppy arrives home, typically at 8 weeks. The 8–16 week window is the most sensitive socialisation period. Enrol in a puppy class within the first two weeks for structured socialisation alongside basic obedience foundations.

faqs.q: How long does it take to train a Working Kelpie?
faqs.a: Working Kelpies can take longer to reach reliable obedience than easier-to-train breeds — expect 3–6 months of consistent daily training for solid basics. Their independent nature means results compound slowly but durably with patience.

faqs.q: What health problems do Working Kelpies commonly have?
faqs.a: Working Kelpies are most commonly associated with routine age-related conditions. Regular vet checks, appropriate weight management, and breed-specific screening tests help detect issues early. Ask any breeder for health test results before purchasing.

faqs.q: How long do Working Kelpies live?
faqs.a: Working Kelpies have an average lifespan of 12–15 years. Good nutrition, appropriate exercise, weight management and regular vet visits are the key factors in achieving the upper end of this range.

faqs.q: Are Working Kelpies prone to hip dysplasia?
faqs.a: Hip dysplasia is less common in Working Kelpies than in large working breeds, but it can still occur. Responsible breeders screen breeding stock. Keeping your Working Kelpie at a healthy weight is the most effective preventive measure.

faqs.q: What health tests should a Working Kelpie puppy have?
faqs.a: At minimum, your Working Kelpie puppy should have a vet health check, first vaccinations, deworming, and microchipping before coming home. Ask the breeder for parent health certificates relevant to Working Kelpie-specific conditions. A vet check within 72 hours of bringing your puppy home is recommended to establish a baseline.

faqs.q: Are Working Kelpies good with kids?
faqs.a: Working Kelpies can be protective and may be cautious around unfamiliar children. Early socialisation with children from puppyhood significantly improves tolerance. Always supervise interactions between dogs and young children.

faqs.q: Do Working Kelpies get along with other dogs?
faqs.a: Working Kelpies can be selective with other dogs due to their protective nature. Early socialisation in puppy classes and controlled on-lead introductions with other dogs help build positive associations.

faqs.q: Do Working Kelpies bark a lot?
faqs.a: Working Kelpies tend to be vocal — they may bark at strangers, sounds, or when under-stimulated. Adequate daily exercise and mental enrichment (training sessions, puzzle feeders) significantly reduce nuisance barking. Teaching a "quiet" cue early is worthwhile.

faqs.q: Are Working Kelpies good apartment dogs?
faqs.a: Working Kelpies can live in apartments if their exercise needs are met consistently. The key variable is owner commitment to daily walks and enrichment — breed size alone doesn't determine apartment suitability.

faqs.q: How much exercise does a Working Kelpie need per day?
faqs.a: Working Kelpies need approximately 60–90 minutes of exercise daily. Split across at least two sessions daily, with one higher-intensity session (running, fetch, swimming) and one loose-lead sniff walk. Mental exercise (training sessions, puzzle feeders) counts toward overall stimulation needs and can reduce restless behaviour.

faqs.q: Are Working Kelpies good running partners?
faqs.a: Yes — Working Kelpies make excellent running partners once fully grown (typically 12–18 months for medium breeds, 18–24 months for large breeds). Start with shorter distances and build gradually to protect developing joints.

faqs.q: What happens if a Working Kelpie doesn't get enough exercise?
faqs.a: Under-exercised Working Kelpies often develop destructive behaviours — chewing, digging, excessive barking, and hyperactivity indoors. These are symptoms of frustration, not bad temperament. Two missed exercise sessions back-to-back typically shows up as restlessness or nuisance behaviour.

faqs.q: Can a Working Kelpie be off-lead?
faqs.a: Working Kelpies can be off-lead in secure areas once recall is reliable. Reliable recall typically takes 3–4 months of consistent training with progressive distance and distractions. Never trust off-lead recall in an unfenced area until it's been tested in controlled conditions first.

faqs.q: How much should I feed my Working Kelpie?
faqs.a: A Working Kelpie needs approximately 1½–3 cups of dry food per day for an adult, split across two meals. Always follow the feeding guide on your specific formula — calorie density varies significantly between brands. Adjust portions based on body condition: you should be able to feel (but not easily see) the ribs.

faqs.q: How many times a day should I feed a Working Kelpie?
faqs.a: Adult Working Kelpies should eat twice daily. Puppies (under 6 months) need 3–4 smaller meals per day to support growth and prevent hypoglycaemia, particularly in small breeds.

faqs.q: What is the best food for a Working Kelpie?
faqs.a: Look for a formula carrying an AAFCO adequacy statement for the correct life stage. A named protein source (chicken, turkey, beef, salmon) should appear first in the ingredient list. Active Working Kelpies benefit from higher-protein formulas (26–30% crude protein) to support muscle maintenance.

faqs.q: When should I switch my Working Kelpie from puppy to adult food?
faqs.a: Most Working Kelpies can transition to adult food between 12 and 15 months. Transition gradually over 7–10 days — mix 25% new food with 75% old food and shift the ratio every 2 days to avoid digestive upset.

faqs.q: Is a Working Kelpie a good dog for first-time owners?
faqs.a: Working Kelpies can be challenging for first-time owners due to their independent temperament. Prior dog experience or professional training classes from the start significantly improves outcomes. Research the breed thoroughly before committing.

faqs.q: Are Working Kelpies good family dogs?
faqs.a: Working Kelpies can be excellent family dogs for active households. They thrive with children who can match their energy level. A calm household with limited exercise may not suit this breed's temperament.

faqs.q: Do Working Kelpies do well when left alone?
faqs.a: Working Kelpies form strong bonds with their owners and do not do well with extended isolation. Aim for no more than 4–6 hours alone at a time. If your schedule requires longer absences, consider a dog walker, doggy daycare, or a companion dog.

faqs.q: How much time do you need for a Working Kelpie?
faqs.a: Plan for 2–3 hours per day dedicated to your Working Kelpie — covering exercise, training, feeding and general interaction.  The commitment is consistent year-round, not just when convenient.
